scenes.title: Cloud Providers: AWS, GCP & Azure
scenes.narration: AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure are the three dominant cloud providers, each offering hundreds of services for compute, storage, and data engineering.

scenes.title: The Big Three
bullets: AWS is the largest and oldest, with the broadest catalog of services and deepest market share.
Google Cloud is known for strong data and analytics tools like BigQuery and its Kubernetes heritage.
Azure integrates tightly with Microsoft enterprises and Active Directory, easing adoption in corporate settings.
scenes.narration: AWS launched first and still offers the widest range of services, making it a safe default. Google Cloud leans into data and machine learning, with BigQuery as a standout analytics engine. Azure wins where organizations already run on Microsoft, thanks to seamless identity and tooling integration.

scenes.title: Naming Across Providers
scenes.narration: Each provider gives similar services different names, which trips up newcomers. Object storage is S3 on AWS, Cloud Storage on Google, and ADLS on Azure. Once you map the concepts across vendors, moving between clouds becomes far less intimidating.

scenes.title: Choosing a Provider
scenes.narration: Provider choice usually starts with what your organization already knows and pays for. From there you compare the specific managed services your pipelines need. Pricing details and the availability of nearby regions often break any remaining tie.

scenes.text: AWS, GCP, and Azure offer the same core building blocks under different names — learn the concepts once and you can work across any of them.
scenes.narration: The three providers share the same fundamental concepts even when the branding differs. Learn object storage, compute, and IAM once, and translating across clouds becomes straightforward.
